title: Bladder / Urothelial Cancer
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: DRAFT decision support authored from standard guidelines (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison) - physician decides. Full pathway for urothelial bladder cancer: initial workup -> disease extent (non-muscle-invasive vs muscle-invasive vs metastatic) -> risk / eligibility stratification (with tables) -> stage-, eligibility-, and line-of-therapy-directed treatment with per-node checklists -> surveillance and recurrence / metastatic pathway. Treatment leaves route to APPLICABLE existing StewardMD Standard Protocols by reference; surgery, radiation, intravesical BCG, and agents with no dose protocol here (carboplatin-gemcitabine, pembrolizumab, erdafitinib, sacituzumab, nadofaragene, adjuvant nivolumab) are shown as checklist guidance with NO dose. Content authored in original wording from general oncology references; no proprietary guideline text reproduced. Invents no dose/regimen. DRAFT - not clinically activated; the physician decides and the existing dose engine computes patient doses.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with standard oncology practice (NCCN / DeVita / Harrison, general references). Regimen options reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols and their own evidence layers; the dose engine computes patient doses.

a.text: High-risk NMIBC that responds to induction BCG is treated with maintenance BCG (a common schedule gives 3 weekly instillations at 3, 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, and 36 months). Maintenance improves recurrence-free and progression-free outcomes over induction alone.

b.text: Common cisplatin-ineligibility criteria (any one): ECOG performance status >= 2, creatinine clearance < 60 mL/min, grade >= 2 hearing loss, grade >= 2 peripheral neuropathy, or NYHA class >= III heart failure. Cisplatin should NOT be replaced by carboplatin in the curative peri-operative setting.

c.text: Switch-maintenance avelumab is offered to patients whose disease has not progressed (complete response, partial response, or stable disease) after 4-6 cycles of first-line platinum-based chemotherapy; it is started within about 4-10 weeks of the last chemotherapy dose.

d.text: Erdafitinib requires a qualifying FGFR2 or FGFR3 alteration (activating mutation or fusion) on molecular testing; monitor for hyperphosphatemia and central serous retinopathy. It is not a substitute for immunotherapy or an antibody-drug conjugate in FGFR-wild-type disease.

nodes.name: Initial workup
nodes.title: Initial workup and staging
nodes.description: Baseline evaluation before treatment. Confirm urothelial histology, define depth of invasion, and stage.

bullets.label: History, physical, and hematuria evaluation
bullets.sub: smoking / occupational exposure, performance status, renal function

bullets.label: Cystoscopy + transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT)
bullets.sub: must sample muscularis propria (detrusor) to assess depth of invasion; re-resect T1 / high-grade / no-muscle specimens

bullets.label: Pathology: grade, depth (Ta / T1 / CIS / >= T2), lymphovascular invasion, variant / non-urothelial histology
Upper-tract imaging with CT / MR urography to exclude synchronous upper-tract disease
Staging for invasive disease: CT chest / abdomen / pelvis; bone scan or targeted imaging if symptoms / alkaline phosphatase
bullets.sub: consider FDG-PET for equivocal nodal / distant disease

bullets.label: Assess cisplatin eligibility (renal function, hearing, neuropathy, performance status, cardiac status) before peri-operative chemotherapy

tables.title: Depth of invasion (simplified T category)
rows: Invades adjacent organs / pelvic or abdominal wall

nodes.name: Disease extent
nodes.title: Disease extent
nodes.description: Management branches first by depth of invasion and spread. Choose the current disease extent.

nodes.name: NMIBC risk group
nodes.title: NMIBC: risk stratification
nodes.description: Risk group drives the intravesical strategy after complete TURBT. Grade, depth, size, multifocality, CIS, and recurrence set the group.

bullets.label: Low
bullets.sub: solitary, primary, low-grade Ta, < 3 cm, no CIS

bullets.label: Intermediate
bullets.sub: low-grade but recurrent / multifocal / > 3 cm; or low-grade T1

bullets.label: High
bullets.sub: any high-grade, any T1, any CIS, or high-grade Ta that is large / multifocal / recurrent

tables.title: NMIBC risk group and default intravesical strategy
rows: TURBT + induction intravesical chemo or BCG

nodes.name: NMIBC low risk
nodes.title: Low-risk NMIBC: TURBT + single instillation
nodes.description: Complete resection with one immediate post-operative intravesical chemotherapy dose; no maintenance.
bullets: Complete TURBT of all visible tumor
Single immediate intravesical chemotherapy (e.g. mitomycin or gemcitabine) within 24 hours of resection
No induction / maintenance course needed for low risk
Surveillance cystoscopy (see follow-up)

nodes.name: NMIBC intermediate risk
nodes.title: Intermediate-risk NMIBC: TURBT + induction intravesical therapy
nodes.description: Complete resection with an induction course of intravesical chemotherapy or BCG.
bullets: Complete TURBT + immediate post-operative instillation
Induction intravesical chemotherapy (mitomycin or gemcitabine), OR induction BCG, based on recurrence risk
Maintenance course for higher-risk intermediate disease
Surveillance cystoscopy (see follow-up)

nodes.name: NMIBC high risk
nodes.title: High-risk NMIBC: TURBT + induction BCG
nodes.description: Restaging (re-)TURBT to confirm no muscle invasion, then induction intravesical BCG; assess response before choosing maintenance vs escalation.
bullets: Re-resection (re-TURBT) of high-grade / T1 tumors before intravesical therapy to confirm depth
Induction intravesical BCG - 6 weekly instillations
Early radical cystectomy is a reasonable alternative for the highest-risk disease (e.g. extensive / multifocal high-grade T1, variant histology, prostatic-urethral CIS)
Assess response at first surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: BCG response
nodes.title: High-risk NMIBC: response to BCG
nodes.description: After induction BCG, response determines maintenance vs bladder-sparing salvage vs cystectomy. BCG-unresponsive disease is a defined high-risk category.
bullets: Cystoscopy + cytology at ~3 months (add upper-tract imaging if positive cytology)
BCG-unresponsive: persistent / recurrent high-grade disease despite adequate BCG (or T1 high-grade at first evaluation)

nodes.name: BCG maintenance
nodes.title: BCG-responsive: maintenance BCG
nodes.description: Continue maintenance BCG with ongoing surveillance.
bullets: Maintenance BCG (3 weekly instillations at set intervals) for 1-3 years
Ongoing cystoscopy + cytology surveillance
Escalate to the BCG-unresponsive pathway on high-grade recurrence

nodes.name: BCG-unresponsive
nodes.title: BCG-unresponsive NMIBC: cystectomy vs bladder-sparing salvage
nodes.description: Radical cystectomy is the standard for fit patients; bladder-sparing options exist for those who decline or are unfit.
bullets: Radical cystectomy + pelvic lymph-node dissection - preferred standard for fit patients

Bladder-sparing salvage (for cystectomy-ineligible / declining, CIS-containing disease): intravesical / systemic pembrolizumab, nadofaragene firadenovec, or the N-803 (nogapendekin) + BCG combination - described as guidance, no dose protocol here
Additional intravesical chemotherapy (e.g. gemcitabine + docetaxel) is an option for selected patients
Close cystoscopic surveillance; low threshold to proceed to cystectomy

nodes.name: MIBC cisplatin eligibility
nodes.title: MIBC: cisplatin eligibility
nodes.description: For non-metastatic muscle-invasive disease, cisplatin eligibility determines whether neoadjuvant chemotherapy precedes definitive local therapy. Cisplatin is not replaced by carboplatin in the curative setting.

nodes.name: MIBC neoadjuvant chemo
nodes.title: MIBC, cisplatin-eligible: neoadjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy
nodes.description: Neoadjuvant cisplatin combination chemotherapy before definitive local therapy improves survival; then choose the local modality.
bullets: Neoadjuvant dose-dense MVAC or gemcitabine + cisplatin (about 3-4 cycles)
Restage after chemotherapy, then proceed to definitive local therapy (next step)
Do not substitute carboplatin for cisplatin in this curative setting
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: MIBC cisplatin-ineligible
nodes.title: MIBC, cisplatin-ineligible: proceed to definitive local therapy
nodes.description: Cisplatin-ineligible patients should not receive neoadjuvant carboplatin; proceed to definitive local therapy, then reassess for adjuvant options.
bullets: No proven benefit from neoadjuvant carboplatin - do not substitute it for cisplatin
Proceed directly to definitive local therapy (next step)
Reassess for adjuvant nivolumab after cystectomy for high-risk pathology
Clinical-trial enrollment (e.g. neoadjuvant immunotherapy) where available

nodes.name: MIBC local therapy
nodes.title: MIBC: definitive local therapy
nodes.description: Choose the definitive local modality: radical cystectomy or bladder-preserving trimodality therapy. Bladder preservation suits selected patients (unifocal T2, no extensive CIS, no hydronephrosis, good bladder function).

nodes.name: Radical cystectomy
nodes.title: Radical cystectomy + pelvic lymph-node dissection
nodes.description: Definitive surgery with bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy and urinary diversion, then adjuvant assessment.
bullets: Radical cystectomy + bilateral pelvic lymph-node dissection
Urinary diversion (ileal conduit or continent / orthotopic neobladder)
Send full pathology (ypT/pT, nodes, margins) to guide adjuvant therapy (next step)
Enhanced-recovery peri-operative care

nodes.name: Trimodality bladder preservation
nodes.title: Bladder preservation: maximal TURBT + concurrent chemoradiation
nodes.description: Organ-sparing trimodality therapy for well-selected patients, with strict cystoscopic surveillance and salvage cystectomy for non-response / recurrence.
bullets: Maximal / complete TURBT of the tumor
External-beam radiation with a concurrent radiosensitizing regimen (e.g. cisplatin, or mitomycin + 5-FU, or low-dose gemcitabine) - radiosensitizer described as guidance
Mid-treatment / post-treatment cystoscopy + biopsy to confirm response
Salvage radical cystectomy for incomplete response or invasive recurrence
Lifelong cystoscopic surveillance (see follow-up)

nodes.name: MIBC adjuvant
nodes.title: MIBC after cystectomy: adjuvant therapy
nodes.description: Adjuvant strategy depends on prior neoadjuvant chemotherapy and surgical pathology risk.

options.label: No prior neoadjuvant + high-risk pathology (>= pT3 or pN+)
High-risk pathology, cisplatin-ineligible or post-neoadjuvant residual

nodes.name: Adjuvant cisplatin chemo
nodes.title: Adjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy
nodes.description: For cisplatin-eligible patients with high-risk pathology who did not receive neoadjuvant chemotherapy.
bullets: Adjuvant cisplatin combination (dose-dense MVAC or gemcitabine + cisplatin) for >= pT3 and/or pN+ disease when no neoadjuvant chemotherapy was given
Only for patients who remain cisplatin-eligible after surgery
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Adjuvant nivolumab
nodes.title: Adjuvant nivolumab (high-risk pathology)
nodes.description: Adjuvant immunotherapy for high-risk muscle-invasive disease after cystectomy, especially cisplatin-ineligible or residual disease after neoadjuvant cisplatin.
bullets: Adjuvant nivolumab (about 1 year) improves disease-free survival for high-risk resected MIBC
Options: cisplatin-ineligible with >= pT3 / pN+, or residual >= ypT2 / ypN+ after neoadjuvant cisplatin
Adjuvant nivolumab regimen referenced below
Monitor for immune-related adverse events

nodes.name: Adjuvant observation
nodes.title: Observation (low-risk pathology)
nodes.description: Organ-confined, node-negative disease - proceed to surveillance without adjuvant systemic therapy.
bullets: No adjuvant systemic therapy for organ-confined (<= pT2), node-negative, margin-negative disease
Structured post-cystectomy surveillance (see follow-up)

nodes.name: Metastatic workup
nodes.title: Metastatic / locally advanced: workup and molecular testing
nodes.description: Confirm extent and obtain predictive biomarkers before selecting first-line therapy.

bullets.label: Cross-sectional restaging (CT chest / abdomen / pelvis); brain / bone imaging if symptomatic
Reassess cisplatin eligibility (renal function, performance status, hearing, neuropathy)
FGFR2 / FGFR3 molecular testing
bullets.sub: identifies candidates for erdafitinib in later lines

bullets.label: Consider PD-L1, HER2 (for trastuzumab deruxtecan / tissue-agnostic use), and MSI / TMB where relevant
Nectin-4 is the target of enfortumab vedotin (not a required predictive test)

nodes.name: First-line strategy
nodes.title: Metastatic first-line: strategy
nodes.description: Enfortumab vedotin + pembrolizumab is the preferred first-line regimen for most patients regardless of platinum eligibility; platinum-based chemotherapy remains an alternative.

nodes.name: EV + pembrolizumab
nodes.title: First-line: enfortumab vedotin + pembrolizumab
nodes.description: Preferred first-line regimen for metastatic urothelial carcinoma; improves survival over platinum chemotherapy.
bullets: Enfortumab vedotin (nectin-4 antibody-drug conjugate) + pembrolizumab
Monitor for EV skin reactions, hyperglycemia, peripheral neuropathy, ocular effects; pembrolizumab immune-related toxicity
Pembrolizumab has no dedicated dose protocol here - shown as guidance; enfortumab vedotin protocol referenced below
On progression, move to the later-line pathway (next step)

nodes.name: Platinum eligibility
nodes.title: Metastatic first-line chemotherapy: cisplatin eligibility
nodes.description: If platinum chemotherapy is chosen, cisplatin eligibility selects the regimen. Cisplatin-ineligible patients receive carboplatin-based chemotherapy.

nodes.name: Cisplatin chemo (metastatic)
nodes.title: First-line, cisplatin-eligible: gemcitabine + cisplatin or ddMVAC
nodes.description: Cisplatin-based combination chemotherapy, then reassess for switch-maintenance immunotherapy.
bullets: Gemcitabine + cisplatin, or dose-dense MVAC, for 4-6 cycles
Assess response and offer switch-maintenance avelumab if no progression (next step)
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Carboplatin chemo (metastatic)
nodes.title: First-line, cisplatin-ineligible: carboplatin + gemcitabine
nodes.description: Carboplatin-based chemotherapy for cisplatin-ineligible patients, then reassess for switch-maintenance immunotherapy.
bullets: Carboplatin + gemcitabine for 4-6 cycles
Assess response and offer switch-maintenance avelumab if no progression (next step)
Carboplatin is used only in the metastatic (non-curative) setting, not peri-operatively
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Maintenance decision
nodes.title: After first-line platinum: response and maintenance
nodes.description: Patients without progression after first-line platinum chemotherapy are offered switch-maintenance avelumab; those who progress move to later-line therapy.

options.label: No progression (CR / PR / stable) after platinum

nodes.name: Avelumab maintenance
nodes.title: Switch-maintenance avelumab
nodes.description: Maintenance immunotherapy after disease control on first-line platinum improves survival; continue until progression / toxicity.
bullets: Avelumab maintenance started within about 4-10 weeks of the last chemotherapy dose
Continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity; monitor for immune-related adverse events
On progression, move to the later-line pathway (next step)
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Later-line option
nodes.title: Metastatic later-line: biomarker / prior-therapy directed
nodes.description: Later-line choice is directed by prior therapy and FGFR status. Avoid repeating an agent class already used first-line.

tables.title: Later-line selection by prior therapy / biomarker
rows: Prior platinum + immunotherapy, no EV yet

nodes.name: Enfortumab vedotin (later line)
nodes.title: Later-line: enfortumab vedotin
nodes.description: Antibody-drug conjugate for patients previously treated with platinum and a checkpoint inhibitor who have not yet received it.
bullets: Enfortumab vedotin (nectin-4 ADC) after prior platinum and immunotherapy
Monitor for skin reactions, hyperglycemia, peripheral neuropathy, and ocular effects
On progression, move to the subsequent-line pathway (next step)
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Pembrolizumab (later line)
nodes.title: Later-line: pembrolizumab
nodes.description: Checkpoint inhibitor for immunotherapy-naive patients after platinum-based chemotherapy.
bullets: Pembrolizumab for immunotherapy-naive disease after platinum chemotherapy
Monitor for immune-related adverse events
On progression, move to the subsequent-line pathway (next step)
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Erdafitinib
nodes.title: Later-line: erdafitinib (FGFR2/3-altered)
nodes.description: Oral FGFR inhibitor for patients with a qualifying FGFR2 / FGFR3 alteration after prior platinum-based therapy.
bullets: Erdafitinib for confirmed FGFR2 / FGFR3 activating mutation or fusion after prior systemic therapy
Monitor phosphate (hyperphosphatemia), ophthalmic exams (central serous retinopathy), nails / skin, and dry mouth
On progression, move to the subsequent-line pathway (next step)
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Later-line other
nodes.title: Later-line: sacituzumab govitecan / single-agent chemotherapy
nodes.description: For patients without an actionable biomarker who have exhausted preferred options.
bullets: Sacituzumab govitecan (Trop-2 ADC) after platinum and immunotherapy - regimen referenced below
Single-agent chemotherapy (e.g. taxane, or gemcitabine if not previously used)
Trastuzumab deruxtecan is an option for HER2-expressing disease (tissue-agnostic) - guidance
Clinical-trial enrollment and best supportive / palliative care as appropriate

nodes.name: Intermediate NMIBC response
nodes.title: Intermediate-risk NMIBC: response after induction
nodes.description: After the induction intravesical course, surveillance cystoscopy and cytology determine whether to continue observation or escalate for recurrence.
bullets: First surveillance cystoscopy + cytology at about 3 months
No recurrence: continue risk-adapted surveillance
Low-grade recurrence: repeat TURBT and consider a maintenance intravesical course
High-grade recurrence or progression to T1 / CIS: manage as high-risk disease (induction BCG or restaging)

nodes.name: Trimodality response
nodes.title: Bladder preservation: response assessment
nodes.description: After maximal TURBT and concurrent chemoradiation, restaging cystoscopy with biopsy (plus cytology and imaging) determines bladder preservation vs salvage cystectomy.
bullets: Restaging cystoscopy + biopsy of the tumor bed after chemoradiation, with cytology and cross-sectional imaging
Complete response: preserve the bladder and enter strict surveillance
Residual muscle-invasive disease or invasive recurrence: prompt salvage radical cystectomy
Non-muscle-invasive recurrence after preservation may be managed with intravesical therapy in selected patients

nodes.name: Bladder preserved
nodes.title: Complete response: bladder-intact surveillance
nodes.description: Complete response to trimodality therapy; preserve the bladder with intensive surveillance.
bullets: Bladder preserved after a complete response to trimodality therapy
Intensive cystoscopy + cytology surveillance, with upper-tract and cross-sectional imaging
Low threshold for salvage cystectomy on muscle-invasive recurrence
Manage non-muscle-invasive recurrence with intravesical therapy where appropriate

nodes.name: Salvage cystectomy
nodes.title: Residual / recurrent disease: salvage radical cystectomy
nodes.description: Salvage radical cystectomy for residual muscle-invasive or invasive recurrent disease after bladder preservation, then adjuvant assessment.
bullets: Salvage radical cystectomy + bilateral pelvic lymph-node dissection and urinary diversion
Higher peri-operative morbidity than primary cystectomy - optimize with enhanced-recovery care
Send full pathology to guide adjuvant assessment (next step)
Consider adjuvant nivolumab for high-risk residual pathology

nodes.name: Trastuzumab deruxtecan
nodes.title: Later-line: trastuzumab deruxtecan (HER2-expressing)
nodes.description: HER2-directed antibody-drug conjugate for HER2-expressing urothelial carcinoma (tissue-agnostic use) after prior systemic therapy.
bullets: Trastuzumab deruxtecan for HER2-expressing (IHC 3+, or IHC 2+) urothelial carcinoma after prior therapy
Monitor for interstitial lung disease / pneumonitis - hold and evaluate any new respiratory symptoms
On progression, move to the subsequent-line pathway (next step)
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Subsequent-line option
nodes.title: Metastatic subsequent-line: after later-line progression
nodes.description: On progression through a later-line agent, choose a subsequent-line option not previously used; prioritize an antibody-drug conjugate or a clinical trial.
bullets: Confirm which agent classes have already been used (platinum, checkpoint inhibitor, enfortumab vedotin, FGFR inhibitor)
Sacituzumab govitecan is a preferred antibody-drug conjugate option after prior platinum and immunotherapy
Enfortumab vedotin if not previously received; erdafitinib if an FGFR2/3 alteration remains untargeted
Otherwise single-agent chemotherapy, a clinical trial, or best supportive care

options.label: Single-agent chemo / clinical trial / best supportive care

nodes.name: Sacituzumab govitecan
nodes.title: Subsequent-line: sacituzumab govitecan
nodes.description: Trop-2 antibody-drug conjugate for previously treated metastatic urothelial carcinoma.
bullets: Sacituzumab govitecan after platinum and a checkpoint inhibitor (typically after enfortumab vedotin)
Monitor for neutropenia (consider growth-factor support) and diarrhea
On further progression, consider a clinical trial or best supportive care
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Trial / supportive care
nodes.title: Subsequent-line: single-agent chemo / clinical trial / supportive care
nodes.description: For heavily pretreated disease without a remaining actionable option.
bullets: Single-agent chemotherapy (e.g. a taxane, or gemcitabine if not previously used)
Clinical-trial enrollment for novel agents or combinations
Integrate palliative and best supportive care; manage symptoms and performance status
Reassess goals of care at each progression

nodes.name: Surveillance
nodes.title: Surveillance / follow-up
nodes.description: Follow-up after treatment; cadence depends on the primary disease extent. Escalate to the metastatic pathway on invasive recurrence.
bullets: NMIBC: cystoscopy + cytology at 3 months, then risk-adapted intervals; periodic upper-tract imaging for high-risk disease
After bladder preservation: cystoscopy + cytology every 3 months initially, with cross-sectional imaging
After cystectomy: cross-sectional imaging and labs (including renal function / B12 for continent diversions) at risk-adapted intervals
Investigate new symptoms; biopsy-proven muscle-invasive or metastatic recurrence enters the metastatic pathway
nodes.linkLabel: If metastatic recurrence is detected: go to the metastatic pathway
